behaviors.given: an afk.json whose mutationReport declares baselinePath "./reports\\mutation\\incremental.json" and decisionsPath "docs/mutation-decisions.json" alongside command and reportPath
behaviors.then: both keys are returned on the parsed mutationReport, normalized by normalizeWaiverPath to forward slashes with no leading ./, and a manifest declaring neither key returns a mutationReport with neither member present
behaviors.observableResult: a unit test on parseAfkManifest asserts toEqual on the returned mutationReport object for both the declared and the undeclared case, and typecheck accepts the optional members on MutationReportDeclaration and MutationReportConfig

behaviors.given: an afk.json whose baselinePath or decisionsPath is a blank string, a glob, an absolute path, or contains a .. segment
behaviors.then: it throws a message naming the offending member and the reason, matching the rule set reportPath already enforces, and afk.json stays at version 1
behaviors.observableResult: it.each cases in src/afk-manifest.test.ts assert expect(() => parseAfkManifest(...)).toThrow(<regex naming the member>) for each refusal of each new key

behaviors.given: an afk.json on disk carrying mutationReport with baselinePath and decisionsPath plus one claimed migration prefix and one unclaimed one
behaviors.then: the bytes on disk still carry both new keys with their original values
behaviors.observableResult: a unit test writes the manifest, calls trimUnclaimedMigrationPrefixes, re-reads afk.json from disk and asserts toEqual including both keys

behaviors.given: decisions-file text that is valid, and text that is not JSON, declares no version 1, holds no decisions array, holds an unrecognized verdict, or holds a blank reasoning; plus a declared baselinePath and decisionsPath where no file exists, and the same paths each occupied by a directory
behaviors.when: parseMutationDecisions parses the text, and readMutationDecisions and readMutationBaseline read each path
behaviors.then: valid text returns status PARSED with the entries keyed as id, file, verdict, consequence, containment and reasoning; every invalid case returns status MALFORMED naming the offending member; a path with no file returns the distinct status ABSENT and a path that exists but throws on read returns UNREADABLE, so absence is never collapsed into a read failure; the baseline is parsed by the existing parseMutationReport on this slice's stated assumption that the tool's incremental artifact is the same mutation-testing-elements document, whose failure mode is contained to BASELINE_UNUSABLE and never a wrong label; nothing ever throws
behaviors.observableResult: unit tests over inline JSON string literals assert the returned status and detail for each parse case with no case wrapped in expect(...).toThrow; separate tests assert ABSENT for a path with no file and UNREADABLE for a path holding a directory, for both readers; and the existing readMutationReport case at src/mutation-report.test.ts:219 still asserts UNREADABLE for a missing report, unedited

behaviors.given: two parsed survivors and a parsed baseline whose survivor set holds one of them at the same file, mutator and identical four position numbers
behaviors.when: attributeMutationSurvivors runs over survivors plus that baseline
behaviors.then: the matched survivor is labeled pre-existing, the unmatched one is labeled new-in-this-run, and the match ignores the tool's per-run mutant id — chosen on this slice's conservative assumption that an incremental file may renumber per-file ids between runs, an assumption that costs nothing if wrong because location and mutator are stable under renumbering either way
behaviors.observableResult: a pure-function unit test asserts the label on each returned survivor, including a case where the baseline holds the same location and mutator under a different id

behaviors.given: a parsed survivor list with, in turn, an omitted baseline argument, a baseline of { status: "ABSENT" }, an omitted decisions argument, and a decisions of { status: "ABSENT" }
behaviors.then: an omitted or ABSENT baseline labels every survivor unattributed and produces no note; an omitted or ABSENT decisions input leaves every baseline label exactly as it is, labels nothing accepted and produces no note; the silent branch is keyed on the omitted-or-ABSENT input alone, so no input satisfies both this behavior and B-08
behaviors.observableResult: a unit test asserts every returned label and an empty notes array for all four cases, including the two decisions cases run against survivors already carrying pre-existing and new-in-this-run baseline labels

behaviors.given: three survivors, a baseline labeling all three, and a decisions document holding an ACCEPT entry matching the first survivor's id and file, an ACCEPT entry whose id matches the second but whose file does not, and a KILL entry matching the third
behaviors.then: the first survivor is labeled accepted in place of its baseline label, the second and third keep their baseline labels, and all three remain in the returned list in their original order; the id-plus-file key is inherited from src/mutation-report.ts:46-50 and ADR 0071 rather than chosen here, and its stated consequence is that a renumbered id makes a committed ACCEPT entry go stale — either matching nothing, so the survivor is re-raised with its baseline label, or matching whichever mutant now holds that id in the same file, so at worst one report bullet is mislabeled, bounded by B-12 because no label reaches a gate, verdict or PR-open condition and an accepted survivor is never removed from the list
behaviors.observableResult: a unit test asserts the three labels and asserts the returned list length and order equal the input's, including the id-matches-but-file-differs case that proves the corroboration

behaviors.given: a parsed baseline plus a decisions input whose status is UNREADABLE and, separately, MALFORMED, and a baseline input whose status is UNREADABLE and, separately, MALFORMED
behaviors.then: the unusable decisions input yields no accepted label, leaves the baseline labels intact and adds the note DECISIONS_UNUSABLE; the unusable baseline labels every survivor unattributed and adds the note BASELINE_UNUSABLE; each note is keyed only on UNREADABLE or MALFORMED and never on the ABSENT or omitted inputs B-06 owns; neither changes the step status away from MUTATION_REPORTED
behaviors.observableResult: unit tests assert the returned labels and notes for all four degraded inputs, assert the notes array is empty for the same call with an ABSENT input, and assert the outcome status stays MUTATION_REPORTED

behaviors.source: GH #304 settled decisions ("report assembly stays a pure function over the parsed survivor list, the optional baseline artifact, and the optional decisions file")
behaviors.given: runMutationStep with a config declaring reportPath, baselinePath and decisionsPath, a stub mutationRun that exits OK, and those three files written under the step's cwd
behaviors.then: the MUTATION_REPORTED outcome carries labeled survivors and the attributionNotes the two files imply, the labels come from one attributeMutationSurvivors call with no extra argument on RunMutationStepArgs, and the abandonment read still sits immediately before the runner invocation with no await between them
behaviors.observableResult: a unit test on runMutationStep asserts the returned outcome's labels and notes, and the existing pre-spawn-window test still passes unchanged

behaviors.source: GH #304 AC2, AC3, AC4, AC5, AC7
behaviors.given: a report whose survivors carry labels new-in-this-run, pre-existing, unattributed and accepted, and whose attributionNotes holds DECISIONS_UNUSABLE
behaviors.then: each survivor bullet keeps its existing id, path, position and mutator text and ends with that survivor's label, and one further line states the degradation, with no per-consumer branch in the formatter
behaviors.observableResult: a unit test asserts the returned string array line by line, and run-summary.md and the draft PR body both render it because both call sites pass through this one formatter

behaviors.given: a ship gate that recorded a mutation-step event and run state record whose survivors carry labels and whose attributionNotes is non-empty, and separately a persisted v7 mutationStep record whose survivors carry no label
behaviors.when: recordMutationStepOutcome writes, run state loads through sanitizeMutationStep, and deriveMutationStepOutcome renders the run summary and readMutationStepOutcome feeds the PR body
behaviors.then: labels and notes survive every hop unchanged, EVENTS_SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1 and RUN_STATE_VERSION stays 7, and the unlabeled legacy record loads unchanged and renders unattributed
behaviors.observableResult: unit tests in src/run-state.test.ts and src/logger.test.ts assert the round-tripped record, the two version constants, and the rendered summary section for both the labeled and the legacy record

behaviors.source: GH #304 AC8; ADR 0063; ADR 0071 "no blocking mutation gate"
behaviors.given: a ship-gate run whose mutation step reported survivors labeled accepted and new-in-this-run
behaviors.when: the gate finishes and assembles its PR creation plan
behaviors.then: its verdict, its gate results and its PR-open decision are identical to the same run whose survivors carry no label, and no gate id, GateDeclaration, GateFindings field, threshold or percentage reads a label or a note
behaviors.observableResult: a ship-gate unit test asserts the two runs' verdict, gate ids, gate outcomes and PR-open decision are equal, and the diff introduces no gate declaration or verdict read touching label or attributionNotes

behaviors.given: a mutation-testing-elements report holding Killed, NoCoverage and Survived mutants, one holding a Survived mutant with no id, mutator or location, and a declared reportPath with no file on disk
behaviors.when: parseMutationReport parses each and readMutationReport reads the missing path

behaviors.observableResult: the report-parser describe at src/mutation-report.test.ts:131 is retitled to carry [behavior:#304:P-06] alongside its current [behavior:#303:B-08] tag — carrying the tag into every assertion inside it, including the missing-file UNREADABLE case at :219 — and its tests pass with fixtures and expectations unedited while the same parser is reused for the baseline artifact
